chunks: Ahmad ibn 'Abdun narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him)
who said regarding taqsir (shortening of prayer): its limit is twenty-four miles.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: taqsir — the juridical act of shortening four-rak'a prayers to two during qualifying travel (qasr al-salat)
key_terms.حَدُّهُ: its limit (hadd) — the precise legal minimum distance threshold
key_terms.مِيلًا: mile (mīl) — a classical unit of distance; in Shia fiqh, 24 miles = 8 farsakhs ≈ 44–48 km

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), what is the minimum travel distance in miles that makes shortening (qasr) of prayer obligatory?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the minimum travel distance triggering the obligation of taqsir — shortening four-unit prayers to two units — is twenty-four miles. This narration is cited in al-Istibsar under the chapter dedicated to the requisite travel distance for qasr, and in Shia fiqh twenty-four miles is understood as equivalent to eight farsakhs, the standard threshold debated across the Four Books.
